newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak crown settles after Czech cbank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Slovak crown settles after Czech cbank intervenes.

text.p: The Slovak crown steadied after sliding in early on Friday with dealers saying Czech central bank intervention on the Czech currency in Prague could boost its Slovak counterpart.
"It seems there will be no dramatic movement as nothing special is happening on the market at the moment," Dusan Svitek of Slovenska Sporitelna said.
In early trading, the crown moved to -0.68 percent against its mark/dollar basket parity after opening at around 55 basis points below the midpoint. It then settled at about -0.63 percent.

Svitek said he expected it might move back to around -0.55 percent, which would pre-empt and Slovak central bank intervention. "But the central bank fixing will be important to this (development)," he added.
On Thursday the NBS fixed the crown/dollar at 32.990, and the crown/mark at 19.542, implying a deviation against the basket of -0.25 percent.
Short-term money market dealers saw the fund rates stable at between 19 to 20 percent, with no sharp changes expected further on Friday.
